review_candidates.title: Senior Director, Global Impact Partnerships
review_candidates.description: At USA for UNHCR, our people are the driving force behind our mission of delivering hope and opportunity to refugees worldwide. We're not just a workplace - we're a vibrant community of passionate, forward-thinking professionals committed to making a real difference. If you thrive in a dynamic, transparent, and data-driven environment, and want your career to directly impact lives across the globe, we invite you to join us! The Senior Director, Global Impact Partnerships is an enterprise leadership opportunity at USA for UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency, to accelerate ambitious growth and translate humanitarian priorities into transformational private-sector engagement. Reporting to the Chief Development Officer, this leader will shape and execute an integrated strategy for partnerships with private-sector organizations headquartered in the United States, including corporations, institutional foundations, civil society and faith-based organizations, community partners, and gift-in-kind partners, while collaborating globally to maximize humanitarian impact. The Senior Director will steward a large, multifaceted team of 12+ fundraising, relationship-management and partnership professionals; strengthen the team’s leadership, collaboration and performance; and create the conditions for talented colleagues to succeed. As a trusted enterprise partner, they will influence strategy and execution across USA for UNHCR, collaborate closely with senior leaders and Board members, and build strong, productive relationships with UNHCR colleagues around the world. The role will deepen and expand complex, multi-year and multimillion-dollar partnerships while opening new pathways for financial support, gifts-in-kind, employee engagement, cause marketing, thought leadership and cross-sector innovation. Through these efforts, the Senior Director will help mobilize resources and relationships that advance UNHCR’s work to save lives, protect rights and build better futures for people forced to flee. Why This Role Matters Now USA for UNHCR is entering an important period of partnership growth, innovation and organizational development. At a time when one in every 70 people worldwide is forcibly displaced, USA for UNHCR has an urgent opportunity to expand the resources, expertise and innovation available to people forced to flee. The Senior Director will build on a uniquely broad portfolio that spans corporations, foundations, civil society, faith communities and gift-in-kind channels to create integrated, transformational partnerships and shape a multiyear growth agenda. By mobilizing financial support, capabilities and cross-sector solutions, this leader will help translate private-sector engagement into lasting humanitarian impact. The Senior Director will have the opportunity to strengthen an established platform, sharpen a multiyear growth strategy, develop leaders across a complex team and deepen collaboration with global colleagues and major partners at a moment of extraordinary humanitarian need. This opportunity is ideal for an accomplished senior partnerships executive from a leading humanitarian, international development or mission-driven organization. The successful candidate will bring external credibility, strategic and commercial judgment, inclusive people leadership and the ability to deliver results through trust and influence in a global, matrixed environment. We recognize that exceptional candidates bring varied experiences and may not meet every listed qualification. If this opportunity aligns with your leadership experience and commitment to people forced to flee, we encourage you to apply. Key Essential Functions And Accountabilities Of The Job Set enterprise partnership strategy. Establish and lead a multiyear strategy across corporate, foundation, civil society, faith-based, community and gift-in-kind partnerships, aligned with USA for UNHCR’s growth priorities and UNHCR’s humanitarian objectives. Drive sustainable revenue growth. Maintain executive accountability for acquisition, retention, expansion, pipeline health, forecasting and delivery against ambitious revenue and partnership goals. Develop transformational partnerships. Guide the cultivation, negotiation and stewardship of complex, integrated, multimillion-dollar and multi-year relationships that mobilize funding, expertise, employee engagement, marketing, thought leadership, advocacy and in-kind resources. Lead and develop the team. Build, coach and retain a high-performing multidisciplinary team; strengthen leadership capacity, clarify accountability, delegate decision-making and foster inclusion, collaboration, learning and sustainable performance. Strengthen global collaboration. Serve as a connector across USA for UNHCR and UNHCR, establishing trusted ways of working, clarifying roles and decision rights, resolving competing priorities and aligning colleagues around shared outcomes. Shape compelling partner propositions. Collaborate with program, stewardship, communications, brand, finance and global colleagues to translate humanitarian priorities into differentiated opportunities and persuasive partner narratives. Provide portfolio and operational leadership. Oversee strategic planning, budgets, forecasts, resource allocation, performance measurement, account planning and data-informed decision-making across the partnerships portfolio. Exercise governance and risk stewardship. Ensure rigorous due diligence, safeguarding, compliance, ethical partnership practices, reputational-risk management and appropriate governance of complex and multi-party agreements. Engage executive and Board leadership. Advise the Chief Development Officer, CEO, Executive Leadership Group and Board on partnership strategy, opportunities, risks, performance and decisions requiring senior sponsorship. Represent USA for UNHCR externally. Serve as a credible senior spokesperson and relationship leader with corporate and foundation executives, humanitarian leaders, peer organizations and other influential stakeholders. Other duties as assigned. Job Requirements Education, Certifications, and Licenses Required Bachelor's degree required; relevant master's degree preferred. Experience Required 12+ years of progressively responsible leadership in partnerships, business development, institutional advancement or resource mobilization, with demonstrated success developing strategy, engaging Boards and leading integrated, multimillion-dollar fundraising programs Demonstrated experience navigating complex, matrixed global organizations Knowledge Of Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Private sector partnership strategy across corporations, foundations, civil society, faith-based organizations, community partners and in-kind channels Integrated and shared-value partnership models that combine philanthropy, business capabilities, employee engagement, marketing, thought leadership, advocacy, and in-kind support. Global humanitarian architecture, refugee and forced-displacement issues, and the roles of UN agencies, NGOs, governments, civil society, and private-sector actors. Revenue growth, pipeline development, portfolio management, partner retention, account planning, and performance measurement. Governance, compliance, due diligence, safeguarding, reputational risk, and ethical partnership practices in complex global organizations. Organizational strategy, change leadership, and decision-making within highly matrixed, multicultural environments. Emerging trends in corporate social impact, institutional philanthropy, innovative finance, impact investing, and cross-sector collaboration. Skills In Setting and communicating a compelling multiyear partnerships strategy linked to organizational and humanitarian priorities. Cultivating, negotiating, securing, and expanding complex, transformational, multimillion-dollar and multi-year partnerships. Leading executive-level engagement with corporate, foundation, nonprofit, UN, and Board stakeholders. Translating technical humanitarian priorities into persuasive investment opportunities, value propositions, proposals, and executive communications. Building alignment across teams with differing priorities, incentives, cultures, and decision-making authority. Exercising sound judgment in partnership governance, due diligence, reputational risk, and complex multi-party agreements. Using portfolio, pipeline, financial, and performance data to allocate resources, assess risk, and drive decisions. Coaching senior leaders and developing high-performing, inclusive, and accountable teams. Ability To Lead a large, multidisciplinary team with clarity, trust, empathy, accountability, and sustainable performance expectations. Influence decisions and align stakeholders across USA for UNHCR and UNHCR without relying solely on formal authority. Establish shared accountability, clarify roles and decision rights, and resolve competing priorities constructively. Build trusted relationships with executive leaders, Board members, global colleagues, partners, and technical experts. Balance ambitious revenue growth with mission integrity, partner value, operational feasibility, and reputational stewardship. Delegate effectively, develop leaders, share information and credit, and create conditions for others to succeed. Invite challenge and diverse perspectives while making timely, well-reasoned decisions in ambiguous circumstances. Lead through organizational change, humanitarian emergencies, and evolving external conditions with resilience and adaptability. Represent USA for UNHCR credibly in high-level external settings and communicate sensitively about displacement and human rights. Foster a culture of collaboration, innovation, inclusion, learning, and accountability. Other Qualifications Demonstrated commitment to refugee protection, human rights, and centering the dignity, agency and perspectives of people with lived experience of forced displacement. Experience leading partnerships or resource mobilization during humanitarian emergencies and/or rapidly evolving external conditions. Experience partnering with UN agencies, global NGOs, country or regional teams, and technical experts across cultures and time zones. Leadership experience in a humanitarian, international development, UN-affiliated, or other complex mission-driven organization strongly preferred. Travel Requirements ☐ Minimal (<10%) ☒ Moderate (10-25%) ☐ Frequent (>25%) Salary New York, NY: $218,765 - $240,888 Washington, DC: $206,596 - $227,488 Work Environment & Physical Demands This position operates in a professional office environment and may be performed in-office, remotely, or in a hybrid setting, depending on organizational requirements and role-specific expectations. Employees are expected to maintain a workspace that supports productive and confidential work, whether on-site or remote. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to communicate and exchange information clearly and effectively. The role is primarily sedentary and involves frequent use of computers and standard office equipment. Tasks may require prolonged periods of sitting and operating technology at a workstation. Occasional movement within the work environment may be necessary. The employee may frequently lift or move items up to 10 pounds and occasionally more without assistance. The typical work environment has moderate noise levels and controlled lighting and temperature. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. Organizational Commitment At USA for UNHCR, we are proud to cultivate a workplace that reflects and respects the rich diversity of the communities we serve. We believe that varied backgrounds, perspectives, and lived experiences make our team stronger, more creative, and better equipped to drive meaningful impact. We are committed to equity and inclusion at every level of our organization. Excellence is not one-dimensional—it emerges through collaboration across lines of difference. We welcome and support employees and candidates of all races, ethnicities, national origins, religions, gender identities, sexual orientations, physical abilities, veteran statuses, and citizenship statuses. We actively encourage individuals from historically underrepresented communities to apply and contribute to our mission of building a world without refugees. Our Values Passionate. The heads and hearts of our team members are committed to our mission Dynamic. We are committed to continuous evolution – finding the best course of action and taking it Transparent. We are open and honest, with each other and with our donors, partners and other stakeholders Cutting Edge. We aspire to be pioneers and find new approaches to connect others with our mission Data Driven. We analyze data, facts and trends to understand our circumstances, and act on what we learn Forward Thinking. We are outcome oriented and focused on what’s ahead Why Join USA for UNHCR? Joining USA for UNHCR means becoming part of a people-first organization that lives its values every day. We're passionate about creating meaningful change, dynamic in our collaborative approach, and transparent in how we work together to support refugees. By embracing cutting-edge solutions and a data-driven mindset, we stay forward-thinking, ensuring your unique talents fuel innovation and impact. Here, you'll grow alongside a supportive team, develop your skills in a nurturing environment, and see the transformative power of your work - on the lives of refugees and on your own journey. Ready to make a difference while being a part of a team that truly cares about you? We'd love to hear from you! Apply today, and let's create a brighter future together.

review_candidates.title: Senior Associate Director - Civil Engineering (Transmission & Distribution)
review_candidates.description: At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good. Your impact Jacobs is playing a leading role in the global energy transition. As our UK and Continental Europe team continues to expand, we are seeking a Senior Associate Director – Civils to provide strategic leadership across frontend engineering design (FEED) and detailed civil/structural design for high-voltage (HV) AIS/GIS substations (132–400 kV), HVDC converter stations, overhead line (OHL) interfaces and underground cable projects. You will shape technical assurance, delivery excellence and market growth in the Transmission & Distribution (T&D) sector. Key Responsibilities Lead civil/structural design packages from concept through detailed design and construction support for National Grid and DNO clients Define civil layouts for substations, including platforms, foundations, bunds, drainage, access roads, ducting, fencing, and security features, integrating geotechnical and structural inputs with electrical plant layouts Drive technical reviews and approvals covering foundation design, structural framing, equipment plinths, transformer bunds/oil containment, flood risk/SuDS, access/haulage, drainage and outfalls Chair design reviews; assure compliance with client procedures Ensure adherence to CDM 2015 and Jacobs’ quality processes Plan resources, programmes and budgets; coordinate with backoffice engineers, subconsultants and suppliers to ensure seamless delivery via common data environments and BIM workflows (e.g., Civil 3D, Revit, MicroStation) Provide construction-phase support (RFI responses, site inspections, NCR closeout), attend site visits, preconstruction reviews and witnessing of civil elements (e.g., foundations, bund systems, drainage structures) Lead and contribute to tenders (technical and commercial), proposals and client presentations; maintain and grow strategic client relationships; position Jacobs in industry forums and standards working groups Line manage and mentor Senior/Principal Engineers; build succession and capability; set technical standards and foster a culture of innovation and excellence Here's what you'll need A degree in Civil Engineering or another relevant engineering discipline Chartered Engineer status with a relevant institution Experience within a civil discipline and experience in delivering complex multi-disciplinary projects for Energy Transition industry Proven leadership of complex, multidisciplinary infrastructure projects within UK T&D, with strong client facing capability Fluency in BIM/CDE processes and design tools (Civil 3D, Revit, MicroStation, Tekla/Tedds), data governance and model assurance Excellent written and verbal communication, stakeholder engagement, and business development acumen; able to manage competing priorities and deliver under pressure Why Jacobs? People are Jacobs’ greatest asset, and we offer a competitive package to retain and attract the best talent. In addition to the benefits you’d expect, UK employees also receive free single medical cover and digital GP service, family-friendly benefits such as enhanced parental leave pay and free membership of employee assistance and parental programmes, plus reimbursement towards relevant professional development and memberships. We also give back to our communities through our Collectively program which incorporates matched-funding, paid volunteering time and charitable donations. #energypowerjobs #ourjacobs #career #opportunity #hybrid #glasgow #manchester #london #exeter #leeds #bristol #reading #energytransition #civilengineering Joining Jacobs not only connects you locally but globally. Our values stand on a foundation of safety, integrity, inclusion and belonging. We put people at the heart of our business, and we truly believe that by supporting one another through our culture of caring, we all succeed. We value positive mental health and a sense of belonging for all employees. With safety and flexibility always top of mind, we’ve gone beyond traditional ways of working so you have the support, means and space to maximize your potential. You’ll uncover flexible working arrangements, benefits, and opportunities, from well-being benefits to our global giving and volunteering program, to exploring new and inventive ways to help our clients make the world a better place. No matter what drives you, you’ll discover how you can cultivate, nurture, and achieve your goals – all at a single global company. Find out more about life at Jacobs. We aim to embed inclusion and belonging in everything we do. We know that if we are inclusive, we’re more connected and creative. We accept people for who they are, and we champion the richness of different perspectives, lived experiences and backgrounds in the workplace, as a source of learning and innovation. We are committed to building vibrant communities within Jacobs, including through our Jacobs Employee Networks, Communities of Practice and our Find Your Community initiatives, allowing every employee to find connection, purpose, and belonging. Find out more about our Jacobs Employee Networks here. Jacobs partners with VERCIDA to help us attract and retain talent from a wide range of backgrounds. For greater online accessibility please visit https//www.vercida.com/uk/employers/jacobs to view and access our roles. As a disability confident employer, we will interview disabled candidates who best meet the criteria. We welcome applications from candidates who are seeking flexible working and from those who may not meet all the listed requirements for a role. We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. We empower employees with our hybrid working policy, allowing them to split their work week between Jacobs offices/projects and remote locations enabling them to deliver their best work. Your application experience is important to us, and we’re keen to adapt to make every interaction even better. review_candidates.title: Rédacteur « réponse d'urgence et partenariats logistiques » (F/H)
review_candidates.description: Description synthétique du poste Au sein du Centre de crise et de soutien (CDCS), le Centre des opérations humanitaire et de stabilisation (COHS) est chargé de la mise en œuvre de l’aide française d’urgence à titre bilatéral, dans les pays en crise et en sortie de crise. Sous l’autorité de la cheffe/du chef du pôle « partenariats et réponse d’urgence », la rédactrice/le rédacteur contribue à l’opérationnalisation de la réponse humanitaire d’urgence de la France. En binôme, elle/il contribue également à la définition stratégique et la mise en œuvre de la préparation à l'urgence (achats, stockages, partenariats, outils...). La rédactrice/le rédacteur est intégré au pôle "affrètement" pour les astreintes et déclenchements de cellule de crise. Activités principales 1- Opérationnalisation de la réponse d'urgence (en lien étroit avec l'unité de réponse d'urgence) : - Analyser les besoins en aide humanitaire en relation avec les Etats demandeurs, les correspondants en ambassade et les capacités de réponse de la France ; - Définir les schémas logistiques et/ou techniques pour chaque opération en coordonnant l’intégralité des acteurs (UE, ambassades, fournisseur, donateur, transitaire, pays récipiendaire, partenaires…) ; - Assurer un lien partenarial (interministériel, privé, ONG, autres Etats...) permettant des opérations conjointes ; - Solliciter les fournisseurs et partenaires pouvant répondre aux besoins définis en assurant le contrôle de la réglementation (document, achats, contrats, prestations, partenariats...) ; - Garantir en interne et en externe, le suivi, la documentation (transport, douanes, règles internationales...), la traçabilité, la redevabilité et les éléments de communication des opérations d'urgences jusqu'au dernier kilomètre incluant les particularités techniques. 2- Préparation à la réponse d'urgence (en lien étroit avec sa/son binôme) : - Définir les prérequis (transports, produits, stockage, capacités...) permettant d'opérer une réponse lors de la survenue d'une crise humanitaire ; - Définir la stratégie partenariale de réponse d'urgence avec les acteurs privés, ONG, interministériels et Etats dans les domaines de la logistique (gestion de stock, du transport...) et des secteurs humanitaires prioritaires (santé, EHA, nutrition...) ; - Définir, améliorer et suivre la stratégie de prépositionnement des stocks et des achats en s'appuyant sur la commande publique et les capacités partenariales ; - Mettre en œuvre la stratégie partenariale en élaborant des conventions de partenariats ; - Contribuer aux réflexions stratégiques sur la réponse d'urgence menées par des acteurs partenaires (UE, ONG, fondations...) ; - Assurer la transmission des informations et garantir l'historique des échanges ; - Créer et assurer le suivi des outils de gestion, de communication, de redevabilité et d’analyse sur les opérations d'urgence, la gestion des stocks et des achats et les partenariats ; - Assurer un partage d’information avec les services internes Diplômes ou expérience professionnelle recommandée pour exercer les fonctions Une expérience dans le secteur de la logistique humanitaire est un pré-requis. Une bonne connaissance des enjeux du secteur et des relations internationales est attendue.

review_candidates.title: Rédacteur zone Europe et référent homologation (F/H)
review_candidates.description: Description synthétique du poste La rédactrice/Le rédacteur assurera le suivi de la zone Europe du Sud (Andorre, Bulgarie, Chypre, Croatie, Espagne, Grèce, Hongrie, Italie, Malte, Monaco, Pologne, Portugal, Roumanie, Saint-Marin, Slovaquie, Slovénie, Tchéquie, Vatican) pour les sujets de politique d’influence dans les domaines de la promotion, la diffusion, l’enseignement du et en français ainsi que du développement de son enseignement. Elle/Il pilotera la campagne interministérielle d’homologation des établissements d’enseignement français pour l’ensemble du réseau en lien avec le Ministère chargé de l’Éducation et l’AEFE. Elle/Il traitera du français dans les organisations internationales, notamment à travers la gestion du programme FIL (Fonds d'intervention linguistique). Activités principales Au sein de la sous-direction de la langue française et de l'éducation, la rédactrice/le rédacteur a la responsabilité du suivi de la zone Europe du Sud pour l'ensemble des sujets relevant de notre politique d’influence dans les domaines de la promotion, de la diffusion et de l’enseignement du et en français ainsi que du développement de l’enseignement français. review_candidates.title: Project Manager TVET
review_candidates.description: We support peace and prosperity by building connections, understanding and trust between people in the UK and countries worldwide. For over 90 years we have shaped brighter futures through education, arts, culture, language, and creativity. We work with people in over 150 countries and reach over 700 million people. We connect. We inspire. British Council Payband 6 Contract Type: Indefinite Contract Location: Uganda Pay Range: 6,626,556 UGA/Monthly Closing Date: 23rd November 2026 at 11:59 pm UGA time / 8:59 pm UK time Please note that candidates are expected to have researched their legal right to live and work in Uganda. Any visa support will be considered at the British Council's discretion. Role Purpose The Project Manager will provide project management and operational support for the development, delivery and evaluation of the British Council's Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) portfolio in Uganda, under the Going Global Partnerships Programme. The role will lead projects from start to finish, managing project plans, contracts, internal and external stakeholders, reporting and compliance requirements. The post holder will build and manage relationships across Uganda's TVET sector, supporting sustainable and impactful programmes aligned with UK sector strengths and expertise. The role will also support institution-to-institution and government-to-government partnerships. Role Context The British Council is the UK's international organisation for cultural relations and educational opportunities, working across arts and culture, English language, education and civil society. Cultural Engagement (CE) brings together the British Council's work in Arts, Education, English & School Education and research, delivering impact through research, sector engagement, policy dialogue and a portfolio of commercial, grant and partnership-funded work globally. The British Council's Education portfolio is organised into three key strands: Student Mobility and Internationalisation, Tertiary Education Partnerships, and Non-formal Education. Through Tertiary Education Partnerships, the British Council facilitates Higher Education, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), and Science Partnerships between the UK and other countries. These partnerships aim to develop high-quality, inclusive and globally connected education systems while sharing UK expertise internationally. The role contributes to the successful delivery of the Education portfolio and strategy by ensuring high-quality project and programme delivery and supporting income generation opportunities in Uganda. Equality, diversity and inclusion are embedded across the British Council's education work to promote respect, inclusion and diversity and ensure mutual benefit for people and partners. Main Accountabilities Relationship and Stakeholder Management Manage relationships with external stakeholders, including the UK tertiary education sector, in-country partners and other relevant stakeholders. Procure services and manage contract delivery partners. Monitor supplier performance and hold suppliers accountable for delivering against contractual requirements. Build and maintain strong internal and external relationships and networks. Commercial and Financial Management Ensure sound financial planning, working closely with finance teams and global programmes to maintain up-to-date British Council and client financial plans. Ensure accurate and timely monthly forecasting by reviewing SAP financial reports, actual expenditure, outstanding purchase orders and commitments. Analyse financial variances against plans and recommend corrective actions. Monitor monthly finances, ensuring expenditure is correctly recorded and the purchase-to-pay (P2P) process is followed. Lead British Council, partner and client reporting, including financial reporting in collaboration with the Finance Manager. Ensure all financial reporting is delivered on time, within budget and to a high standard. Ensure compliance with British Council financial policies and procedures. Project Management Contribute to the development and delivery of the Project Management Plan. Identify project and programme risks and develop mitigation strategies in collaboration with the Senior Responsible Officer (SRO). Manage internal and client requirements relating to procurement, contracting, compliance and reporting. Ensure reports submitted by grant recipients, consultants and external providers are complete, comprehensive and of high quality. Manage project and programme procurement in line with required standards and processes. Oversee data management, including timely data entry, quality assurance, basic analysis of monitoring data and progress reporting to meet funding requirements. Coordinate programme-specific data collection, working with colleagues to identify appropriate indicators and tools and ensuring data quality. Business Development Support the development of commercial proposals, ensuring equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) and gender-sensitive programming are integrated. Work with relevant business support teams to ensure proposals are appropriately costed and priced. Ensure timely reporting and communication on externally funded contracts, grant-funded initiatives and internal monthly reporting. Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) Actively contribute to an inclusive and anti-racist organisational culture, recognising personal biases and taking action to address them. Promote an environment where people feel valued and are treated equitably, supporting well-being and mental health. Apply the British Council's approach to equality, diversity and inclusion in day-to-day work. Embed good EDI practices across Education projects and programmes, ensuring design and delivery contribute positively to gender equality, disability and social inclusion. Role Specific Knowledge And Experience Minimum / Essential Requirements Experience of managing projects from start to finish and familiarity with project life cycles. Understanding of project procurement, evaluation and reporting requirements. Proven experience of managing project finances. Experience of managing stakeholders. More than two years' experience in project or programme management. Experience of using technology in project delivery. Good understanding of and experience in supporting monitoring and evaluation. Degree or equivalent experience. Desirable Requirements Experience and understanding of the tertiary education sector. Project management qualification or equivalent relevant experience. Language Requirements Written and verbal proficiency in English is required. Additional Job Requirements Candidates are expected to have researched their legal right to live and work in Uganda. Any visa support will be considered at the British Council's discretion. Initial and continuing employment with the British Council is subject to an annual background check. Candidates should demonstrate alignment with British Council values: Open and Committed; Expert and Inclusive; Optimistic and Bold. A connected and trusted UK in a more connected and trusted world. Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Statement We are committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and we welcome applications from all sections of the community as we believe that a diverse workforce gives added depth to our work. The British Council is a Disability Confident Employer. The Disability Confident scheme helps challenge attitudes, increase understanding of disability, and ensure staff are drawn from the widest possible pool of talent and we guarantee an interview for disabled applicants who meet the minimum role requirements. We welcome discussions about specific requirements or adjustments to enable participation and engagement in our work and activities. Safeguarding Statement The British Council is committed to safeguarding children, young people, and adults who we work with. We believe that all children and adults everywhere in the world deserve to live in safe environments and have the right to be protected from all forms of abuse, maltreatment and exploitation as set out in article 19, UNCRC (United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child) 1989. Appointment to positions where there is direct involvement with vulnerable groups will be dependent on thorough checks being completed in line with legal requirements and with the British Council’s Safeguarding policies for Adults and Children. If you experience any difficulties with submitting your application, please email askhr@britishcouncil.org

review_candidates.title: Program Manager, HIV Prevention
review_candidates.description: The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems. CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally. At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work http//www.clintonhealthaccess.org CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture. Program Overview Lenacapavir (LEN) is a long-acting injectable HIV prevention product given twice a year. Clinical trials show near-complete protection against HIV, and the twice-yearly dosing can help people who struggle to take daily oral PrEP. In Indonesia, the HIV epidemic is concentrated among key populations, while recent reductions in external HIV funding have put prevention programs at risk. With funding from GiveWell, CHAI will run a 2.5-year implementation research program to support the introduction of LEN in Indonesia about 12 months of preparation, followed by 18 months of implementation research. The program aims to reach around 7,000 people from key populations (men who have sex with men, transgender women, people who inject drugs, and female sex workers) across about 20 sites in West and East Java, through community/private clinics and key-population-friendly Puskesmas. The evidence on uptake, continuation, cost, and acceptability will inform the Ministry of Health's (MoH) decisions on national scale-up, policy inclusion, and sustainable financing. The program is organized around four workstreams Regulatory and ethics secure LEN approval through BPOM’s Special Access Scheme and ethical approval of the study protocol Commodities procure LEN and distribute it to study sites without stockouts Service delivery and demand prepare sites, train health workers and civil society organizations, and generate demand among key populations Data and evidence build the M&E framework with the MoH and SI PrEP/SIHA, and collect and analyze routine data, provider surveys, and key informant interviews Position Overview The Program Manager will lead CHAI's day-to-day design, delivery, and learning for the Lenacapavir program in Indonesia. The Program Manager will manage the full project cycle across all four workstreams, lead a small team (a Program Officer and a Senior Admin, Logistic and Data Assistant), serve as the main point of contact for the MoH, BPOM, provincial and district health offices, partners, and the donor. They will also ensure the program generates the evidence and government ownership needed for national scale-up. They are expected to influence program strategy, build relationships with senior stakeholders, and operate independently with strong technical and strategic judgment. Program leadership and delivery Lead the program through its phases preparation (regulatory and ethics approval, procurement, M&E set-up, and training), implementation research, and dissemination of results. Translate the proposal into a detailed workplan with clear milestones, owners, and risk mitigation; track progress against the workplan, budget, and indicators, and recommend course corrections to senior management and the donor. Anticipate and manage key risks, such as regulatory or ethics delays, product availability, and lower-than-expected uptake or continuation. Lead, mentor, and set priorities for the program team; supervise consultants and partners; and manage matrixed support from CHAI’s global and regional teams. Government and stakeholder engagement Build and maintain trusted relationships with the MoH, BPOM, ethics committees, provincial and district health offices in West and East Java, study sites, and community and key population networks. Represent CHAI in HIV prevention and PrEP technical working groups, and coordinate with development partners to align efforts. Prepare clear briefs, presentations, and recommendations for senior government and donor audiences. Technical delivery and evidence generation Lead the BPOM Special Access Scheme application and the study protocol and ethics approval process, working with regulatory consultants, research partners, and CHAI’s global team. Oversee LEN procurement, importation, and distribution to study sites, making sure supply matches enrolment and that clients can receive their continuation doses on time. Work with the MoH to develop the M&E framework and adapt SI PrEP/SIHA so that LEN uptake and continuation can be tracked, and use routine data to drive reviews with sites and district teams. Oversee site readiness, health worker and CSO training, and demand generation activities that are sensitive to the needs of key populations. Lead analysis of study findings and turn them into policy briefs and recommendations on national guideline inclusion, scale-up, and domestic financing, and share lessons with CHAI Vietnam and regional forums. Budget and donor management Manage the program budget, forecast spending, and monitor burn rate. Ensure compliance with donor and CHAI financial and fiscal requirements. Prepare timely, accurate narrative and financial inputs to donor reports. Master's degree in public health, epidemiology, health policy, medicine, pharmacy, or a related field. A bachelor's degree with significantly more experience or a degree in management and business with extensive health-related implementation research experience may be considered. At least five to seven years of progressive experience managing health programs, including leading multiple workstreams or a medium-to-large project from planning through closure. Demonstrated experience in HIV programs, ideally HIV prevention or PrEP. Experience working with government counterparts, preferably the Indonesia MoH or provincial and district health offices. Demonstrated ability to manage budgets and donor requirements, and to supervise and develop professional staff. Ability to engage sensitively and without stigma with key populations. Excellent written and spoken English and Bahasa Indonesia, including the ability to prepare polished briefs and present to senior audiences. Willingness to travel regularly to West and East Java. Advantages Experience with new product introduction, implementation or operational research, or study design. Experience with BPOM regulatory or ethics approval processes in Indonesia. Familiarity with SI PrEP, SIHA, or other national health information systems. Experience with health commodity procurement and supply chain. Experience working with community-based organizations or key population networks. #jobreference3 #region2
